get.description:
Returns the caller org's headline aggregate plus a per-kind
breakdown — the observatory's poll target. Canonical and retained counts travel
together, so a deduped view never reads as loss. ?project= narrows to one project.

parameters.name: project
parameters.description: Project narrows the aggregate to one project. Empty aggregates the whole org.

get.summary: GetResearchXP computes the deterministic, non-transferable Hanzo XP read projection (HIP-1402) from canonical qualified EvolutionCandidates and independently replicated confirmatory ResearchClaims.
get.description:
GetResearchXP computes the deterministic, non-transferable Hanzo XP read
projection (HIP-1402) from canonical qualified EvolutionCandidates and
independently replicated confirmatory ResearchClaims. Unqualified proposals,
exploratory runs, and unreplicated claims yield strictly zero XP, and any
retracted claim or candidate emits a compensating negative projection that
reverses the credit to net zero.

parameters.name: project
parameters.description: Project narrows the projection to one project; empty folds the whole org.

parameters.name: principal
parameters.description: Principal narrows to one principal (did:hanzo:... or user id).

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: Domain narrows to one skill domain (harness, engine, model, sandbox, science, spec).

code.description: A stable token a client can branch on, when the refusal names one.

detail.description: What was refused, for a person to read.

action.description:
Action is the DDT Action, verbatim: id, decisionId, status, verdict, rule,
description. Its id is required; its status, when present, must be DRAFT;
and it carries no authorizedBy or authorizedAt, which are the server's.
Authorizing writes AUTHORIZED into it.

assignee.description: Assignee is who the action is assigned to.

authorizedAt.description: AuthorizedAt is when it was authorized, RFC 3339 UTC. The server's.

authorizedBy.description: AuthorizedBy is the person who authorized it. The server's.

by.description: By is the user who filed this state. The server's.

decisionId.description: DecisionID is the DDT Action's decisionId. DERIVED by the server.

hash.description:
Hash is this state's content hash, lowercase hex, over the DDT Action, the
assignee and the authorization. Authorizing names it, so a person
authorizes the state they read. The server's.

id.description:
ID is the action's record id, `act_` and 32 hex digits, one per DDT Action
id. The server's.

status.description:
Status is DRAFT until a person authorizes the action, then AUTHORIZED. The
server's: a write files DRAFT, and a DRAFT never replaces an AUTHORIZED
action.

time.description:
Time is when this state of the action was filed, RFC 3339 UTC. The
server's.

answer.description:
Answer is what the model answered, after the harness extracted it from the
raw generation.

benchmark.description:
Benchmark is the suite the item belongs to — gpqa_diamond, livecodebench.
Part of the stable id (project, benchmark, item, model). Required on ingest.

correct.description:
Correct is the producer's grade of Answer against Gold. This plane records
the verdict and re-grades nothing, so it is only ever as good as the
harness that sent it.

gold.description: Gold is the expected answer for the item, as the benchmark states it.

item.description:
Item is the one question or case that was scored, by the benchmark's own
id for it. Part of the stable id. Required on ingest.

model.description: Model is what answered the item. Part of the stable id. Required on ingest.

received_at.description:
ReceivedAt is the server wall-clock timestamp (unix seconds) stamped when
this attempt version was first recorded. Ignored on ingest.

response.description:
Response is the raw generation the model produced. It is its own retention
class — it may carry personal or licensed material — and it is part of the
version's content identity, so a re-run that produced different text is a
new retained version.

revision.description:
Revision is the producer's declared kind of this version: original,
corrected or retracted. Anything else, including empty, is read as
original. A retracted latest version withdraws the item's canonical answer;
every earlier version stays retained.

source.description:
Source names who measured this attempt. Empty is recorded as
hanzo-measured; any other value is stored as sent, so an imported
third-party score is distinguishable from one this fleet ran.

status.description:
Status is this attempt's execution state, the same vocabulary a run uses:
empty is complete, faulted retains a negative result, and an unrecognized
value is kept verbatim. faulted and failed are excluded from the answered
counts but never dropped.

ts.description:
TS is when the attempt was measured, unix SECONDS. Display-only: a
server-assigned append clock, not this, decides which version is canonical.
Defaults to ReceivedAt when 0 on ingest.

principal.description: Principal is the contributing human or agent identity (did:hanzo:... or user id).

weight.description: Weight is this contributor's fractional share; shares across a record sum to 1.0.

attested_at.description: AttestedAt is the RFC 3339 UTC timestamp when the attestation was recorded.

evidence_ref.description: EvidenceRef is the content-addressed Evidence or Run digest verified.

role.description: Role names the attestation stage: harness, qualifier, or promoter.

signature.description: Signature is the optional cryptographic signature (ed25519:...) over candidate_id.

verifier.description: Verifier is the independent principal attesting to the candidate's evaluation.

complete.description:
Complete: the run says it answered every question it set out to and says
when it ended.

inconsistent.description: Inconsistent: the run's own two counts cannot both be true.

partial.description:
Partial: the run says it answered fewer. A number taken from one of
these was taken from a checkpoint.

unknown.description:
Unknown: the run does not establish completion. This is the common case
for anything recorded before a lane wrote its counts, and it is reported
rather than rounded toward either of the other three.

criteria.description: Criteria are what the options are judged by.

due.description: Due is when the decision is due.

owner.description: Owner is who owns the decision.

question.description:
Question is what the decision answers, in a sentence. Required when a
charter is sent.

scope.description: Scope is what the decision covers.

agreed.description:
Agreed reports whether the replication satisfied directional and interval
agreement with the primary claim.

confidence_hi.description: ConfidenceHi is the optional upper confidence bound reported by the replication run.

confidence_lo.description: ConfidenceLo is the optional lower confidence bound reported by the replication run.

replicated_at.description: ReplicatedAt is the RFC 3339 UTC server timestamp when this replication was recorded.

run_id.description: RunID is the completed independent Run that reproduced the primary claim.

value.description: Value is the measured value observed on the replication run for the claim's metric.

verifier.description:
Verifier is the independent principal (distinct from the claim's proposer)
who executed and filed this replication.

by.description: By is the person who committed. The server's.

decisionId.description: DecisionID is the DDT decision committed. It must be filed. Required.

evaluationHash.description:
EvaluationHash is that filing's hash, recorded by the server. When sent it
must be the named filing's (409 otherwise).

evaluationId.description:
EvaluationID is the evaluation filing the commitment rests on, by its
record id. When sent it must be filed, for the same decision.

id.description: ID is the commitment's record id, `com_` and 32 hex digits. The server's.

note.description: Note is what the person wants on the record beside it.

selection.description: Selection is the option committed to. Required.

time.description: Time is when they committed, RFC 3339 UTC. The server's.

a.description: A is the first run, canonical version, as a read returns it.

blocks.description:
Blocks are the reasons these two runs are not comparable, each in a
sentence — a different benchmark, a different split, different dataset
bytes, or either run not established as complete. Empty means none was
found, which is not a guarantee of comparability: it is the absence of
the failures this record can see.

comparable.description:
Comparable is true only when Blocks is empty. It is the single bit a
caller should branch on before rendering a delta.

config.description:
Config is every configuration field the two runs disagree about, whether
or not they are comparable. A comparable pair with a long Config list is
the normal case — it is what the pair is FOR — and reading a delta
without reading this is how a prompt change gets published as a model
improvement.

deltas.description:
Deltas are the per-(category, metric) changes over what both runs
measured, ordered by category then metric. A metric only one of them
reported is left out rather than compared against nothing.

evidence_ref.description:
EvidenceRef is the content-addressed Evidence or artifact digest (sha256:...
or ev_...) demonstrating the refutation or regression.

filed_at.description: FiledAt is the RFC 3339 UTC server timestamp when the retraction was recorded.

filed_by.description: FiledBy is the principal who submitted the counter-evidence.

run_id.description:
RunID is the optional completed Run ID whose negative or contradictory
measurement refuted the claim.

summary.description: Summary states concisely how the prior claim or candidate failed verification.

by.description: By is the user who filed it. The server's.

charter.description: Charter is the decision's charter, when one is filed with it.

decision.description:
Decision is the DDT-1.0 Decision record, stored verbatim. The server checks
that schemaVersion is "DDT-1.0" and that id is present. A version that
changes lifecycleState, agentPermissions, or any member the newest
version's agentPermissions.mayNotChange names is a person's to file: any
other caller is refused 403. Required.

decisionId.description:
DecisionID is the DDT decision's id: the record's `id` member, trimmed —
the same reading ?decision= and a commitment's decisionId get. The server's.

depends.description:
Depends is every evidence uri the decision names — its `evidence` and each
assumption's `evidence` — once each, with a hash where the record gives one.
DERIVED by the server.

id.description: ID is this version's record id, `dec_` and 32 hex digits. The server's.

program.description: Program is the Decision Program bound from the decision, when one is.

supersedes.description:
Supersedes is the record id of the version this one follows. Empty on the
first. The server's.

time.description: Time is when this version was filed, RFC 3339 UTC. The server's.

version.description: Version is this version's ordinal for its DDT id: 1, 2, … The server's.

visibility.description:
Visibility is private, org or public. A write records private; a grant
(POST /v1/research/grants, kind decision, the DDT id) moves every version.

a.description: A is the first run's value.

b.description: B is the second run's value.

category.description: Category is the slice both runs measured this metric on.

change.description:
Change is B minus A, in the metric's own unit. Nothing is normalized and
nothing is turned into a percentage, so a change is only ever as
meaningful as the two values it came from.

metric.description: Metric is the quantity, in whatever unit both runs reported it.

overlap.description:
Overlap says whether the two reported intervals overlap. Null means at
least one run reported no interval, so nothing is claimed. True means the
change is inside the noise BOTH runs already declared, which is the
answer most published deltas actually have.

hash.description:
Hash is the version the record read, lowercase hex. Empty when the record
names the uri and no version of it.

decisionId.description: DecisionID is the DDT decision it belongs to.

hash.description:
Hash is the version of the evidence it read, lowercase hex. Empty when it
names the uri and no version.

id.description: ID is its record id: the decision version's, or the evaluation's.

stale.description: Stale is true when Hash is not the uri's newest version.

a.description:
A is the field's value on the first run, rendered as text. An empty
string is the record not saying; it is distinguished from a value of
"0" or "false".

b.description: B is the same field's value on the second run.

field.description:
Field is the configuration field, by its wire name: reader, k,
dataset_digest.

by.description: By is the user who filed it. The server's.

decisionId.description:
DecisionID is the DDT decision evaluated. Taken from the Evaluation Run's
decisionId when absent; the two must agree when both are sent.

depends.description:
Depends is every uri the evaluation read, with the hash it read: the
package's evidence, or without a package the Evaluation Run's inputs.
DERIVED by the server: a depends sent with the record must name exactly
those, in any order.

evaluationRun.description:
EvaluationRun is the DDT Evaluation Run, verbatim: id, evaluator, inputs
(uri → hash) and outputs. Its id is required. A run is bound to one
package: every filing of one run id names the same outputs.hash (409
otherwise), and an id beginning RUN_KAI_ is Kai's name for that package,
RUN_KAI_ and the first 16 hex digits of outputs.hash, uppercased (422
otherwise). With a package its outputs.hash must be the package's hash, and
its inputs, when sent, exactly the evidence the package read.
outputs.readiness, when sent, is DDT's readiness result:
{decisionClassPolicyId: string, verdict: string or null}, its verdict the
package's.

hash.description:
Hash is this filing's content hash, lowercase hex, over its decision id and
the canonical JSON of its Evaluation Run and package. A commitment resting
on the evaluation records it. The server's.

id.description:
ID is this filing's record id, `eval_` and 32 hex digits, over the
Evaluation Run id and the filing's hash: the same run filed with other
content is another evaluation, and both are kept. The server's.

package.description:
Package is Kai's full Decision Package, verbatim. Its `hash` is required
and must be its content hash as Kai computes it: the SHA-256 of the
canonical JSON of every member but hash and trace. It is kept in the
hash-addressed blob store.

recommendation.description:
Recommendation is lifted from Package: its selection, ranking, flips and
readiness. DERIVED by the server; absent without a package.

time.description: Time is when this evaluation was filed, RFC 3339 UTC. The server's.

visibility.description:
Visibility is private, org or public. A write records private; a grant
(POST /v1/research/grants, kind evaluation, the Evaluation Run id) moves
every filing of it.

by.description: By is the user who filed this version. The server's.

content.description:
Content is the evidence itself, any JSON value of at most 16 MiB, kept in
the hash-addressed blob store. Required: the server files what it hashed
and nothing it did not. Only GET /v1/research/evidence/{id} and the write
that filed it answer it; a listing leaves it out.

hash.description:
Hash is the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the content's canonical JSON (keys
sorted, no whitespace, shortest numbers — the form DDT and Kai hash). The
server computes it; a hash sent beside the content must agree. A `sha256:`
prefix is accepted and dropped.

id.description:
ID is this version's record id, `ev_` and 32 hex digits. The server's; a
write ignores it.

kind.description:
Kind is requirement, test, model, analysis, document, or element for a
SysML element. Required.

links.description: Links are its typed edges to other evidence, by uri.

source.description: Source is the system the evidence was read from.

time.description: Time is when this version was filed, RFC 3339 UTC. The server's.

uri.description:
URI is the evidence's stable name, the key its versions accrue under. A
SysML element's is sysml://<project>@<commit>#<elementId>. Required.

version.description:
Version is this version's ordinal for its uri: 1 for the first content
filed under it, then one more for each filing whose hash is not the uri's
newest. The server's.

visibility.description:
Visibility is private, org or public. A write records private; a grant
(POST /v1/research/grants, kind evidence, the uri as its id) moves every
version.

artifact_digest.description:
ArtifactDigest is the content-addressed digest (sha256:...) of the mutated
artifact bundle.

attestations.description: Attestations lists independent verification and qualification attestations.

candidate_id.description:
CandidateID is the sha256:<hex> digest of the canonical candidate payload
(excluding signature, attestations, and mutable lifecycle fields).

contributors.description: Contributors holds fractional attribution shares summing to 1.0 for XP projection.

created_at.description: CreatedAt is the RFC 3339 UTC timestamp when the candidate was proposed.

diff_ref.description: DiffRef is the content-addressed unified diff or patch bundle against parent_ids[0].

evidence_refs.description:
EvidenceRefs lists content-addressed Evidence or Run digests produced by
evaluating this candidate.

evolution_fitness.description: EvolutionFitness holds optional Level 2 meta-evolutionary yield and lift metrics.

gate_ref.description:
GateRef names the evaluation benchmark or conformance suite version gating
this candidate.

mutation_surface.description:
MutationSurface names the single permitted architectural surface modified:
harness.policy, engine.strategy, router.cascade, model.adapter, or research.protocol.

parent_ids.description:
ParentIDs lists one or more parent candidate_ids (or ["root"] for genesis
baselines), forming a directed acyclic lineage graph.

product_fitness.description: ProductFitness holds the Level 1 multi-objective task metrics once evaluated.

project.description:
Project is the sub-scope inside the org this candidate belongs to, set by
the server on write.

proposer.description: Proposer is the principal (did:hanzo:... or IAM user) proposing the candidate.

qualified_at.description: QualifiedAt is the RFC 3339 UTC timestamp when the candidate was qualified.

qualified_by.description: QualifiedBy is the independent principal who qualified or promoted the candidate.

retracted_by.description: RetractedBy holds the CounterEvidence digest when status is retracted.

rollback_target.description:
RollbackTarget is the pinned parent candidate_id or artifact digest preserved
for instant rollback on promotion (HIP-1401 §5.2).

seq.description: Seq is the store's monotone append sequence number for this version.

signature.description: Signature is the proposer's optional cryptographic signature over candidate_id.

spec_version.description:
SpecVersion is the target Hanzo OS standard.json semantic version (for
example "1.0.0").

status.description: Status is proposed, qualified, promoted, retired, or retracted.

was_qualified.description:
WasQualified records whether this candidate passed independent qualification
before any subsequent retraction, enabling exact XP reversal.

discovery_rate.description:
DiscoveryRate is the fraction of generated child candidates that pass
independent holdout qualification.

reproducibility.description:
Reproducibility is 1.0 minus variance across independent clean-room reruns
in [0.0, 1.0].

research_yield.description: ResearchYield is verified fitness delta achieved per US dollar of compute spent.

successor_lift.description:
SuccessorLift is the best verified fitness improvement over parent lineage
within a fixed compute horizon.

transfer_rate.description:
TransferRate is the fraction of improvements on source tasks that transfer
without regression to out-of-distribution target tasks.

canonical.description:
Canonical is DERIVED on read, never stored and never taken from an upload:
a version is canonical when it is the latest-appended non-retracted version
of its stable id. The listing returns only canonical versions, so it is
true on every row it answers with.

content_hash.description:
ContentHash is the server-computed SHA-256 identity over the version's
measurement, provenance, and canonicalized tags. Ignored on ingest; returned
on reads.

cost_usd.description:
CostUSD is what the run cost in US DOLLARS (not cents), as the producer
reports it. It is summed as-is into the per-project and per-kind totals.

endpoint.description:
Endpoint is the optional BYO URL naming the arm the run measured. It is
checked at ingest — https only, and every address the host resolves to must
be publicly routable — and then dropped: nothing stores it, no read returns
it, and this plane never dials it.

git_branch.description: GitBranch is the branch that commit was on.

git_dirty.description:
GitDirty says the working tree carried uncommitted changes, so GitSHA does
not fully describe what ran.

git_sha.description:
GitSHA is the commit the run was measured at. Provenance is part of the
version's content identity, so the same number measured on a different
commit is a new RETAINED version rather than an idempotent no-op.

id.description:
ID is the run's stable id, `<kind>:<subject>:<task>` by convention. It is
the key versions accrue under: a correction re-sent with this same id
appends a new version beside the old one rather than replacing it.
Required on ingest.

kind.description:
Kind is the discriminator the whole plane is partitioned by: benchmark,
kernel-perf, training, ablation, policy-eval, or ab for an A/B trial's
per-arm evidence. Required on ingest, and open — an unknown kind is stored,
not refused.

lib_versions.description:
LibVersions is the libraries in force, as a JSON object of name → version
({"harness":"0.1.0"}). It is a queryable column and part of the content
identity, which is what makes "which lib version regressed this task"
answerable over the longitudinal record. Absent is {}.

meta.description:
Meta is whatever else the producer wants to carry, as a JSON object — the
A/B rows put lift, z and p here. It is part of the version's content
identity, canonicalized (sorted keys, no whitespace) first so that a
re-serialization of the same object does not mint a spurious version.
Absent or unparseable is stored as {}.

metric.description:
Metric names the quantity Value carries — accuracy, tok/s, a conversion
event. It is the only place Value's unit is stated; this plane declares no
vocabulary of metrics.

n.description:
N is the sample size behind Value — items scored, or exposures for an A/B
arm.

n_total.description:
NTotal is the denominator the producer reports N against — the size of the
set N was drawn from. The plane derives neither from the other, so a
producer that reports only N leaves this 0.

project.description:
Project is the sub-scope inside the org this run is filed under. On ingest
it is the SERVER's value — the caller's project scope — and a project sent
in the body is ignored; on a read it is the value the run was filed under.

publishable.description:
Publishable is consent to publish this run to the commons. Ingest forces
false; only a grant sets it.

received_at.description:
ReceivedAt is the server wall-clock timestamp (unix seconds) stamped when
this version was first recorded. Ignored on ingest and excluded from
ContentHash so re-ingesting identical content stays idempotent.

revision.description:
Revision is the producer's declared kind of this version: original,
corrected or retracted. Anything else, including empty, is read as
original. A retracted latest version WITHDRAWS the id — it has no canonical
version at all — and every earlier version is still retained.

seq.description:
Seq is the server-assigned monotone append clock stamped when this version
was recorded. Ignored on ingest; returned on reads so supersession order is
externally auditable.

status.description:
Status is the run's execution state: planning, running, complete or
faulted. Empty is complete (a backfilled historic run). An unrecognized
value is kept verbatim rather than flattened, so a producer's own failure
label is never displayed as a success. faulted and failed runs are retained
but are left out of the answered headline counts.

subject.description:
Subject is what was measured: the model, the engine, the A/B arm. Required
on ingest.

tags.description:
Tags are optional producer labels attached to the experiment, canonicalized
as sorted unique strings on write and queryable via ?tag= on GET /v1/research/experiments.
Included in ContentHash only when non-empty so pre-existing untagged hashes never move.

task.description:
Task is what it was measured ON — gpqa_diamond, livecodebench, prefill, or
the trial's id for A/B evidence.

trainable.description:
Trainable is consent to train on this run. Ingest forces false; only a
grant sets it. An upload conveys no training right.

ts.description:
TS is when the run was measured, unix SECONDS. When 0 on ingest, the server
defaults it to ReceivedAt so newly recorded runs always carry a timestamp,
while Seq and ReceivedAt provide server-authoritative ordering.

value.description:
Value is the measurement, in whatever unit Metric names. It is NEVER
normalized: one producer files accuracy as 0.81 and another as 94.3 and
both are stored as sent, so compare values only within one (subject, task,
metric).

visibility.description:
Visibility is private, org or public. Ingest forces private whatever the
body says; only a grant moves it.

canonical.description: Canonical is true on the single latest non-retracted version of the stable id and false otherwise.

content_hash.description: ContentHash is the server-computed SHA-256 identity over the measurement, provenance, and tags.

git_sha.description: GitSHA is the commit SHA recorded on this version.

meta.description: Meta is the canonicalized metadata JSON object recorded on this version.

n.description: N is the sample size recorded on this version.

received_at.description: ReceivedAt is the server wall-clock timestamp (unix seconds) when this version arrived.

revision.description: Revision is the producer's declared version kind: original, corrected, or retracted.

seq.description: Seq is the per-org monotone append clock stamped when this version was recorded.

status.description: Status is the run's execution state on this version (planning, running, complete, faulted, ...).

tags.description: Tags are the canonicalized sorted unique labels recorded on this version.

ts.description: TS is the producer's measured-at timestamp (unix seconds), defaulted to ReceivedAt when omitted.

value.description: Value is the measured quantity recorded on this version.

field.description:
Field is the run field, by its wire name — so a reader goes straight
from this list to the field on the run that is missing.

runs.description: Runs is how many of the runs do not state it.

id.description:
ID addresses an experiment (run) by its stable id — or a decision by its
DDT id, an evaluation by its Evaluation Run id, evidence by its uri, which
take visibility only and are not narrowed by project. The grant lands on
EVERY retained version of that id, because the decision is about the record
and not about one version of it.

kind.description:
Kind names what ID addresses: run, decision, evaluation or evidence. Empty
when the id names records of one kind alone; an id that names records of
more than one kind is refused 409 without it, so a grant never moves a
record it did not name.

project.description:
Project locates WHICH project inside the caller's org holds the target;
empty is the caller's own project scope. It is not a tenant key — the org
comes from the validated principal — so naming a project can only ever
address a record the caller's org already owns.

publishable.description:
Publishable is consent to publish the run to the commons. Null leaves it
unchanged; an artifact grant ignores it.

sha256.description:
SHA256 addresses an artifact by its content hash instead, and an artifact
grant sets visibility only. One of ID and SHA256 is required; when both are
sent SHA256 wins and the run is untouched.

trainable.description:
Trainable is consent to train on the run's records. Null leaves it
unchanged; an artifact grant ignores it.

visibility.description:
Visibility is private, org or public. Null leaves it unchanged, and it is
the one field an artifact grant requires.

max_compute_seconds.description:
MaxComputeSeconds is the maximum wall-clock or sandbox compute budget in
seconds permitted for one confirmatory execution; 0 leaves duration unbounded.

max_cost_usd.description:
MaxCostUSD is the maximum spend in US dollars permitted for one confirmatory
execution; 0 leaves dollar spend unbounded.

budget.description: Budget bounds the compute seconds and US dollar cost allowed for confirmatory runs.

dataset_refs.description:
DatasetRefs lists the content-addressed dataset digests (sha256:...) fixed
before execution begins.

gate_ref.description:
GateRef names the evaluation benchmark or gate suite (for example
benchmark://swe-bench-verified@1.2.0 or a ResearchBenchmark id).

hypothesis_id.description:
HypothesisID is the content-addressed sha256:<hex> digest of the canonical
hypothesis specification, computed inside the trust boundary.

null_hypothesis.description: NullHypothesis states the condition under which the hypothesis is falsified.

project.description:
Project is the sub-scope inside the org this hypothesis belongs to, set by
the server from the caller's project scope on write.

proposer.description:
Proposer is the human or agent principal (did:hanzo:... or IAM user) filing
the hypothesis; stamped from the authenticated caller when omitted.

registered_at.description:
RegisteredAt is the RFC 3339 UTC server timestamp when this hypothesis was
recorded.

seq.description:
Seq is the store's monotone append sequence number establishing strict
pre-registration ordering before confirmatory runs.

statement.description: Statement is the falsifiable claim predicting a measurable directional effect.

hip.description: HIP is the four-digit zero-padded HIP identifier (for example "1401").

version.description: Version is the semantic version of that HIP's contract implemented here.

category.description: Category is the measure's category, exactly as recorded in the run.

direction.description: Direction is higher or lower; improvement is signed in this direction.

max_regression.description: MaxRegression is the greatest permitted degradation for this metric.

metric.description: Metric is the measure's name, exactly as recorded in the run.

min_gain.description: MinGain is the primary metric's required absolute gain in its own units.

baseline.description: Baseline is the reference run id, in this study's project and study.

metrics.description: Metrics are the objective followed by optional regression guardrails.

min_questions.description: MinQuestions is the minimum completed evaluation size (at least one).

require_intervals.description:
RequireIntervals blocks a verdict unless both runs report non-overlapping
intervals for the primary metric. Intervals must use the same method.

target.description: Target names the harness, app, skill, connector or infrastructure under test.

attempts.description:
Attempts are the per-item attempt versions. Each needs a benchmark, an item
and a model. The two arrays may not BOTH be empty, and they hold at most
20000 members between them — split a larger upload.

experiments.description:
Experiments are the run versions in this batch. Each needs an id, a kind
and a subject. Re-sending byte-identical content appends nothing.

cost_usd.description: CostUSD is US DOLLARS (not cents) summed over those same runs.

experiments.description:
Experiments counts the canonical answered runs of this kind — the same
predicate as the headline count, sliced.

kind.description:
Kind is the discriminator this row aggregates: benchmark, kernel-perf,
training, ablation, policy-eval, ab. A kind appears as soon as any RETAINED
version carries it, so a kind whose every run was retracted or faulted is
listed with zero experiments rather than dropped.

rel.description:
Rel is the edge: satisfies, verifies, derives, supersedes, refines or
dependsOn.

uri.description: URI is the evidence the edge points at.

category.description:
Category is the slice of the run's items this number covers: all, dev,
test, multi-hop, mh_32k. "all" is the whole run.

hi.description: Hi is the high end of that same interval. Null on the same terms as Lo.

lo.description:
Lo is the low end of the interval the harness reported around Value.
Null means it reported none — NOT an interval of zero width, which is
what a bare 0 would claim.

metric.description:
Metric is the quantity — f1, em, recall@10, substring_em. It is the only
place Value's unit is stated; nothing here normalizes, so one harness's
0.45 and another's 45.1 are both stored as reported and are comparable
only within one (benchmark, metric).

n.description:
N is how many items this number was computed over. Null means the
harness did not say, which is the difference between a wide interval and
an unknown one.

of.description:
Of is how many items the category HOLDS — the denominator N is drawn
from. Null means the harness did not say. N far below Of on a run whose
completion reads complete is the sign of a category the run skipped
rather than failed.

value.description: Value is the number, in whatever unit Metric names.

category.description: Category is the slice of the run's items this number covers.

hi.description: Hi is the high end of that interval. Absent when it reported none.

lo.description:
Lo is the low end of the interval the harness reported. Absent when it
reported none.

metric.description: Metric is the quantity, and the only place Value's unit is stated.

n.description:
N is how many items this number was computed over. Absent when the
harness did not say.

of.description:
Of is how many items the category holds. Absent when the harness did not
say.

value.description: Value is the number, in whatever unit Metric names.

authors.description: Authors are its authors, in the order they are credited.

canonical.description:
Canonical is DERIVED on read: the latest-appended non-retracted version
of this id.

cites.description:
Cites are the Run ids the paper's claims rest on. This is the whole
point of the type: a paper that quotes a number names the execution it
came from, and that execution's completion can then be checked.

doi.description: DOI is its DOI, when it has one.

id.description: ID is the paper's stable id, a slug or a HIP number. Required on a write.

project.description:
Project is the sub-scope inside the org this paper is filed under — the
SERVER's value on a write.

revision.description:
Revision is this version's declared kind: original, corrected or
retracted, on the same terms as every other record here.

status.description:
Status is where the writing has got to: draft, preprint, published or
withdrawn. It is free text beyond those — an unrecognized value is kept
verbatim rather than flattened, so a producer's own label is never shown
as something it did not say.

study.description: Study is the Study id this paper reports, when it reports one.

url.description: URL is where it can be read.

venue.description: Venue is where it appeared, or is to appear.

when.description:
When is when the paper was recorded, RFC3339. Empty means the record does
not say.

cost_per_success_usd.description:
CostPerSuccessUSD is total token plus sandbox compute spend in US dollars
per verified task success (minimize).

latency_p50_ms.description: LatencyP50Ms is median wall-clock task completion latency in milliseconds (minimize).

latency_p95_ms.description: LatencyP95Ms is 95th-percentile wall-clock task completion latency in milliseconds (minimize).

robustness.description:
Robustness is the pass rate under adversarial perturbation and environment
variation in [0.0, 1.0] (maximize).

safety.description:
Safety is 1.0 minus the policy/sandbox violation rate in [0.0, 1.0]; must
equal 1.0 (zero violations) for qualification.

verified_success.description:
VerifiedSuccess is the pass rate on deterministic conformance and holdout
suites in [0.0, 1.0] (maximize).

hash.description:
Hash is the bound program's hash, lowercase hex. A `sha256:` prefix is
accepted and dropped.

id.description: ID is the program's id, apu.select.

attempts.description:
Attempts counts the CANONICAL answered attempts, one per (benchmark, item,
model).

attempts_retained.description:
AttemptsRetained counts every attempt version held, on the same terms as
ExperimentsRetained.

benchmarks.description: Benchmarks is how many DISTINCT benchmarks those same attempts cover.

cost_usd.description:
CostUSD is US DOLLARS (not cents) summed over the canonical answered runs,
so it is what the deduped view cost and not what the history cost.

experiments.description:
Experiments counts the CANONICAL answered runs: one per stable id, the
latest non-retracted version, faulted and failed left out.

experiments_retained.description:
ExperimentsRetained counts every run version the store holds for the
project — superseded and retracted included. Retained is always ≥
canonical, and the gap is history rather than loss.

kinds.description:
Kinds are the discriminators seen in the project, sorted, over ALL retained
versions — so a kind stays listed after its runs are superseded or
retracted, even when it contributes nothing to Experiments.

models.description:
Models is how many DISTINCT models appear across the canonical answered
attempts.

project.description:
Project is the project these totals cover. Rows are one per project the org
has evidence under, sorted by this.

decisionClassPolicyId.description:
DecisionClassPolicyID is the decision class policy ruled on, as the
Evaluation Run's outputs.readiness names it.

verdict.description:
Verdict is the join of the sealed package's gate verdicts: allow, ask or
deny. Empty when no gate rules.

flips.description: Flips are the parameter values at which the top option changes, verbatim.

ranking.description: Ranking is the package's ranking of the options, verbatim.

readiness.description:
Readiness is DDT's readiness result: the package's joined gate verdict on
the decision's class policy. Absent when the package has no verdict and the
Evaluation Run names no policy.

selection.description: Selection is the option the package selects. Empty when it selects none.

created_at.description: CreatedAt is the RFC 3339 UTC timestamp when the regression was first captured.

error_signature.description: ErrorSignature is the normalized failure fingerprint or invariant identifier.

failing_run_id.description: FailingRunID is the optional Run ID or trace digest that exhibited the error.

fix_candidate_ref.description:
FixCandidateRef names the qualified EvolutionCandidate (sha256:...) that
resolved the regression.

gate_test_ref.description:
GateTestRef names the deterministic regression test added to the evaluation
gate so the failure can never recur silently.

project.description:
Project is the sub-scope inside the org this regression belongs to, set by
the server on write.

regression_id.description: RegressionID is the content-addressed sha256:<hex> identity of the captured failure.

reported_by.description: ReportedBy is the principal or daemon that captured the failure.

seq.description: Seq is the store's monotone append sequence number for this version.

source_kind.description:
SourceKind classifies where the failure originated: eval_failure,
production_error, counter_evidence, or conformance_failure.

status.description:
Status is captured (error recorded), gated (reproduction test wired), or
fixed (qualified candidate verified against the gate test).

summary.description: Summary describes the failure mode and reproduction condition.

updated_at.description: UpdatedAt is the RFC 3339 UTC timestamp of the latest transition.

artifact_id.description:
ArtifactID is an optional producer-assigned logical identifier for the artifact
(e.g. "manifest-v1" or "rotten-tomatoes-predictions").

canonicalization.description:
Canonicalization names the byte-canonicalization scheme applied by the producer
before hashing (e.g. "rfc8785-jcs" or "utf8-lf"), when applicable.

content.description:
Content is the artifact's bytes, base64, on WRITE only, at most 16 MiB.
Never returned: a read answers metadata and the address, and the bytes come
from GET /v1/research/artifacts/{sha256}.

git_branch.description: GitBranch is the branch that commit was on.

git_dirty.description: GitDirty says the working tree carried uncommitted changes.

git_sha.description:
GitSHA is the commit that produced the artifact. Unlike a run's, an
artifact's provenance is NOT part of its identity: the bytes are.

kind.description:
Kind classifies the artifact: snapshot, report (default when omitted), artifact,
evidence, harness, manifest, or result.

lib_versions.description:
LibVersions is the libraries in force, as a JSON object of name → version.
Absent is {}.

media_type.description:
MediaType is the MIME type of the stored bytes (e.g. "application/json",
"text/markdown", "image/png"). Validated on write and served on blob reads
when in the safe non-script allowlist.

project.description:
Project is the project the artifact is filed under — the SERVER's value on
write. It is part of the read predicate too: fetching a hash from the wrong
project is the same 404 as a hash that was never recorded.

received_at.description:
ReceivedAt is the server wall-clock timestamp (unix seconds) stamped when
the artifact was first recorded. Ignored on write.

ref.description:
Ref is the content address, "sha256:<hash>", composed by the server from
the same bytes. A ref sent in the body is discarded, so it can never name
somewhere else.

retention_class.description:
RetentionClass is the retention bucket the bytes fall in. Every write is
recorded as raw-artifact — the class for material that may be personal or
licensed — so it is the server's word, not the caller's.

run_id.description:
RunID is the experiment stable id this artifact belongs to, which is what
the diary feed's ?run= filters on. It is free text: nothing checks that the
run exists.

sha256.description:
SHA256 is the SERVER's hash of the submitted bytes, hex, and the artifact's
identity — the key the blob route is addressed by. A caller MAY send one;
it is not trusted, only checked, and a mismatch with the bytes refuses the
write.

ts.description:
TS is when the artifact was recorded, unix SECONDS — what the feed sorts
newest-first on and what ?since= is compared against. Defaults to ReceivedAt
when 0 on write.

uncompressed_size.description:
UncompressedSize is the uncompressed byte length of the artifact; defaults to
len(rawBytes) on write when omitted or zero.

visibility.description:
Visibility is private, org or public. A write forces private; only a grant
by sha256 moves it.

canonical.description:
Canonical is DERIVED on read, never stored: a version is canonical when
it is the latest-appended non-retracted version of its id. A listing
returns only canonical versions, so it is true on every row it answers
with.

citation.description:
Citation is how to cite the task: the paper, the arXiv id, the
repository. A benchmark without one is a number nobody can check back to
a definition.

dataset.description:
Dataset is the items the benchmark draws on, named the way the reader
fetches them: a Hugging Face path, a repository, a file.

id.description:
ID is the benchmark's stable id, lowercase and terse: locomo, mab,
repobench-r. It is what a Run's `benchmark` names and what versions of
this definition accrue under. Required on a write.

license.description:
License is the terms the DATASET comes under — CC BY-NC 4.0, MIT. Empty
means the record does not say, which is not the same as permissive; a
benchmark whose licence is unrecorded is one nobody has checked.

metric.description:
Metric is the OFFICIAL metric — the one the benchmark's authors score it
by and the one a comparison against published numbers has to use.

metrics.description:
Metrics are every quantity the benchmark's protocol reports, official
one included. A run may measure more; it may not measure fewer and still
claim the benchmark.

notes.description:
Notes is anything about the task a reader needs and the fields above do
not carry — that the released items are a proxy for an unreleased set,
say.

origin.description:
Origin is where the dataset was obtained: the URL or repository it was
fetched from. Provenance for the items themselves, distinct from
Citation, which is provenance for the task.

project.description:
Project is the sub-scope inside the org this definition is filed under.
On a write it is the SERVER's value — the caller's project scope — and a
project sent in the body is ignored.

revision.description:
Revision is this version's declared kind: original, corrected or
retracted. Anything else, including empty, reads as original. A retracted
latest version WITHDRAWS the id; every earlier version stays retained.

splits.description:
Splits are the divisions the benchmark declares, each with its own
definition. A run names one of these in its `split`.

title.description: Title is the benchmark's published name, as its authors write it.

version.description:
Version is the benchmark's OWN revision — v6, 2025-03 — not the version
of anything that ran it. Empty means the benchmark publishes none.

when.description:
When is when this definition was recorded, RFC3339. Empty means the
record does not say.

candidate_ref.description:
CandidateRef is the optional EvolutionCandidate digest (sha256:...) evaluated
by this claim.

claim_id.description:
ClaimID is the content-addressed sha256:<hex> identity of the claim's core
assertion, computed by the server.

confidence_hi.description: ConfidenceHi is the optional upper confidence interval bound for Value.

confidence_lo.description: ConfidenceLo is the optional lower confidence interval bound for Value.

contributors.description: Contributors holds optional multi-principal attribution shares summing to 1.0.

counter_evidence.description: CounterEvidence holds the refutation record when status is retracted.

created_at.description: CreatedAt is the RFC 3339 UTC timestamp when the claim was first filed.

effect_size.description: EffectSize is the directional delta over the baseline or null threshold.

evidence_refs.description: EvidenceRefs lists content-addressed Evidence or artifact digests backing the claim.

hypothesis_id.description:
HypothesisID is the pre-registered HypothesisRecord (sha256:...) this claim
tests; required when mode is confirmatory.

metric.description: Metric names the measured quantity on the primary and replication runs.

mode.description:
Mode is confirmatory (pre-registered before execution) or exploratory
(post-hoc observation, ineligible for confirmatory promotion or XP).

project.description:
Project is the sub-scope inside the org this claim belongs to, set by the
server on write.

proposer.description: Proposer is the principal filing the claim.

replications.description: Replications lists independent replication attempts recorded against this claim.

run_id.description: RunID is the completed primary Run ID supporting this claim.

seq.description: Seq is the store's monotone append sequence number for this version.

status.description:
Status is unreplicated, replicated, or retracted — derived and enforced by
the server's verification state machine.

updated_at.description: UpdatedAt is the RFC 3339 UTC timestamp of the latest state transition.

value.description:
Value is the primary run's measured value on Metric, derived from the run
record when present.

was_replicated.description:
WasReplicated records whether this claim ever achieved independent
replication prior to a retraction, so XP reversal is auditable.

attempts.description:
Attempts counts the CANONICAL answered attempts, one per (benchmark, item,
model).

attempts_retained.description:
AttemptsRetained counts every attempt version held, on the same terms as
ExperimentsRetained.

benchmarks.description: Benchmarks is how many DISTINCT benchmarks those same attempts cover.

by_kind.description: ByKind is the same headline split per discriminator, ordered by kind.

cost_usd.description: CostUSD is US DOLLARS (not cents) summed over the canonical answered runs.

experiments.description:
Experiments counts the CANONICAL answered runs: one per stable id, the
latest non-retracted version, faulted and failed left out.

experiments_retained.description:
ExperimentsRetained counts every run version held — superseded and
retracted included. Retained is always ≥ canonical, and the gap is history
rather than loss, which is why both travel together.

models.description:
Models is how many DISTINCT models appear across the canonical answered
attempts.

project.description:
Project echoes the project the aggregate was narrowed to. Absent means the
figures below span the whole org.

projects.description:
Projects is how many DISTINCT projects the counted evidence spans, so it is
1 whenever Project narrows to one.

answered.description:
Answered is how many of them it actually answered. Null means the record
does not say. Below Questions the run is partial; above it the two
counts contradict each other and the run is inconsistent.

baseline.description:
Baseline marks a run as the reference the others are read against. It
changes nothing about how the run is stored or compared; it is how a
board knows which line to draw first.

benchmark.description:
Benchmark is the ResearchBenchmark id this run measured against. Nothing
checks that the definition is recorded — a run may be filed before its
benchmark is — but a comparison across two different values here is
refused.

by.description:
By names who ran it: the person, the job, the fleet. Empty means the
record does not say.

canonical.description:
Canonical is DERIVED on read, never stored: a version is canonical when
it is the latest-appended non-retracted version of its id.

commit.description:
Commit is the commit the harness was frozen at. Together with the
digests above and the knobs beside them it is what "re-runnable from its
own record" means.

completion.description:
Completion is DERIVED on read from Questions, Answered and Ended, and is
never stored or taken from a write: complete, partial, inconsistent or
unknown. It is the field a published number must be checked against.

dataset_digest.description:
DatasetDigest is the sha256 of the dataset the run scored against. It is
the strongest single guard on comparability: two runs over different
dataset digests measured different items.

embedder.description:
Embedder is the embedding model the run retrieved with. Empty means the
record does not say, or the run retrieved nothing.

ended.description:
Ended is when it stopped, RFC3339. Empty means the record does not say
it ever did — which alone keeps completion at unknown, however well the
counts agree.

facts_digest.description:
FactsDigest is the sha256 of the extracted-fact layer the run retrieved
over, for runs that have one.

id.description:
ID is the run's stable id — the run directory's name by convention,
`<benchmark>-<split>-<config>-<system>`, carrying no date. It is the key
versions accrue under: a correction re-sent with this id appends a new
version beside the old rather than replacing it, which is how a run
published from a checkpoint is fixed without erasing what was published.
Required on a write.

k.description:
K is the retrieval depth. Null means the record does not say — never 0,
which would claim the run retrieved nothing.

key.description:
Key is the measurement's identity, DERIVED on read and never taken from
a write: sha256 over what decides the number — benchmark, split, system,
version, k, temperature, max_tokens, embedder, reader and the four
digests — and over nothing about who ran it, when, at which commit or
what it found. Two runs with one key measured the same thing, so a
harness asks ?key= before it spends and measures again only when told to.

max_tokens.description:
MaxTokens is the reader's answer cap. Null means the record does not
say.

measures.description:
Measures are the run's numbers, one row per (category, metric), with the
intervals the harness reported.

notes.description:
Notes is anything about this execution a reader needs that no field
above carries — a fallback that was hit, a category that was skipped.

project.description:
Project is the sub-scope inside the org this run is filed under. On a
write it is the SERVER's value — the caller's project scope — and a
project sent in the body is ignored.

prompt.description:
Prompt is the prompt FILE the run read, by path. The file is what makes
a prompt reproducible; the digest below is what makes it checkable.

prompt_digest.description:
PromptDigest is the sha256 of that file's bytes as the harness recorded
it. Two runs whose prompt digests differ read different instructions,
whatever their prompt paths say.

publishable.description:
Publishable is consent to publish this run to the commons. A write forces
false; only a grant sets it.

questions.description:
Questions is how many questions the run set out to answer — the
DENOMINATOR. Null means the record does not say, and a run that does not
say cannot be shown as finished. This field and the next are why this
type exists.

reader.description:
Reader is the model that produced the answers. Empty means the record
does not say; the literal `none` means the run measured retrieval and
read nothing.

revision.description:
Revision is this version's declared kind: original, corrected or
retracted. Anything else, including empty, reads as original. A
retracted latest version WITHDRAWS the id; every earlier version stays
retained.

split.description:
Split is which of the benchmark's declared splits the run covered.
Empty means the record does not say, and two runs cannot be compared
across differing splits.

store_digest.description:
StoreDigest is the sha256 of the retrieval store the run queried —
the index, with whatever was in it.

study.description:
Study is the Study id this run belongs to, when it belongs to one. A run
names its study; it never names a paper.

system.description:
System is what was under test — the model, the engine, the retrieval
policy. A baseline names its system here like any other run:
`naive-rag` is a system that was measured, never a category inside
somebody else's numbers. Empty means the record does not say, which a
comparison treats as a reason not to compare rather than as a match.

temperature.description:
Temperature is the reader's sampling temperature. Null means the record
does not say — never 0, which is a deliberate and common setting and so
the most expensive possible default.

trainable.description:
Trainable is consent to train on this run. A write forces false; only a
grant sets it. Recording a run conveys no training right.

version.description:
Version is the system's own version at the time it was measured. Empty
means the record does not say, and two runs of one system at unrecorded
versions are not known to be two runs of the same thing.

visibility.description:
Visibility is private, org or public. A write forces private whatever the
body says; only a grant moves it.

when.description:
When is when the run started, RFC3339. Empty means the record does not
say. It is what ?since= and ?until= bound a listing by.

answered.description:
Answered is how many of them it answered. Null means the record does not
say.

baseline.description: Baseline marks the run the others are read against.

benchmark.description: Benchmark is the task the run measured against.

canonical.description: Canonical is true on every row a listing answers with.

commit.description: Commit is the commit the harness was frozen at.

completion.description:
Completion is derived from Questions, Answered and Ended: complete,
partial, inconsistent or unknown.

ended.description:
Ended is when the run stopped, RFC3339. Empty means the record does not
say it ever did.

id.description: ID is the run's stable id.

measures.description: Measures are the run's numbers, narrowed as the query asked.

notes.description: Notes is anything about the execution no field above carries.

project.description: Project is the sub-scope inside the org the run is filed under.

questions.description:
Questions is how many questions the run set out to answer. Null means the
record does not say.

revision.description:
Revision is this version's declared kind: original, corrected or
retracted.

split.description:
Split is which of the benchmark's splits the run covered. Empty means the
record does not say.

study.description: Study is the study the run belongs to, when it belongs to one.

system.description: System is what was under test. Empty means the record does not say.

version.description:
Version is the system's version when it was measured. Empty means the
record does not say.

visibility.description: Visibility is private, org or public.

revision.description:
Revision is that system's own revision of what was read: a SysML commit,
a PLM baseline. Empty when the system has none.

system.description: System names the system of record: sysml, ddt, plm, techdata. Free text.

definition.description:
Definition is the split in the benchmark's own words — "conversations 0,
1 and 2", "the 32k, 64k and 262k haystacks". It is what makes a split
reproducible by someone who has only the dataset, so a split named
without one is a label rather than a definition.

items.description:
Items is how many of the benchmark's items the split holds. 0 means the
definition does not state a size.

name.description: Name is what the benchmark calls this division: dev, test, all.

capabilities.description: Capabilities lists the HIP-0139 capability identifiers served here.

component.description: Component is the canonical layer and component identifier (research/cloud).

implemented_hips.description: ImplementedHIPs lists every HIP specification this component implements.

spec_version.description: SpecVersion is the target Hanzo OS standard.json semantic version.

version.description: Version is this component's semantic release version.

canonical.description:
Canonical is DERIVED on read: the latest-appended non-retracted version
of this id.

finding.description:
Finding is what the runs showed, once they had. Empty while the study is
open — and a finding recorded before the runs completed is the failure
this whole record exists to make visible.

id.description:
ID is the study's stable id, a slug. Runs name it in their `study`.
Required on a write.

improvement.description:
Improvement enables automatic, deterministic review of this study's runs.
Every candidate is compared with the named baseline using these declared
metrics; results become private DRAFT research actions, never deployments.

project.description:
Project is the sub-scope inside the org this study is filed under — the
SERVER's value on a write.

question.description:
Question is what it set out to answer, in a sentence. A study without
one is a folder.

revision.description:
Revision is this version's declared kind: original, corrected or
retracted, on the same terms as every other record here.

title.description: Title is what the study is called.

when.description:
When is when the study was opened, RFC3339. Empty means the record does
not say.

domains.description:
Domains maps each active skill domain (harness, engine, model, sandbox,
science, spec) to its net verified integer XP.

principal.description: Principal is the human or agent identity whose verified reputation this summarizes.

total_xp.description: TotalXP is the sum of net verified XP across all six domains.

candidate_ref.description:
CandidateRef is the EvolutionCandidate or ResearchClaim digest that earned
or lost this XP.

delta.description:
Delta is the signed integer XP change (positive on verified qualification
or replication, negative on retraction reversal).

domain.description:
Domain is one of the six closed skill domains: harness, engine, model,
sandbox, science, or spec.

effective_at.description: EffectiveAt is the RFC 3339 UTC timestamp of the underlying verification or retraction.

evidence_ref.description: EvidenceRef is the Evidence or Run digest backing this XP entry.

principal.description: Principal is the human or agent identity receiving this non-transferable delta.

projection_id.description:
ProjectionID is the deterministic sha256:<hex> digest of
(evidence_ref, principal, domain, reason, rule_version).

reason.description: Reason is candidate_qualified, claim_replicated, conformance_resolved, or retracted.

retracted_by.description:
RetractedBy names the CounterEvidence digest when this credit was reversed,
or null/empty while active.

rule_version.description: RuleVersion is the semantic version of the pure XP projection function ("1.0.0").

data.description: Data are the actions, newest first, each in its latest state.

artifact_id.description: ArtifactID echoes the optional logical artifact identifier when supplied.

content_sha256.description: ContentSHA256 echoes the server-verified SHA-256 hex digest of the raw bytes.

created.description: Created is false when these exact bytes were already recorded — the write is a no-op.

kind.description: Kind is the normalized artifact kind recorded on the store ("report" when omitted).

media_type.description: MediaType echoes the normalized MIME type when supplied.

received_at.description: ReceivedAt is the server wall-clock timestamp (unix seconds) when the artifact was first stored.

rolled_up.description: RolledUp is false when the OLAP roll-up was skipped; the SQLite write still stands.

sha256.description: SHA256 is the SERVER's hash of the bytes — the artifact's identity.

uncompressed_size.description: UncompressedSize is the recorded uncompressed byte length.

data.description: Data are the artifacts, newest first. Content bytes are never returned here.

ID.description: ID is the action's record id, in the path.

hash.description:
Hash is the hash of the state the person read: the action's `hash` as a
listing answered it. Required.

benchmarks.description:
Benchmarks are the definitions to record. Each needs an id. At most
20000 in one call.

data.description: Data are the canonical benchmark definitions, ordered by project then id.
Data are the matching canonical EvolutionCandidates.
Data are the canonical ResearchClaims, newest sequence number first.
Data are the commitments, newest first.
Data are the decision versions, newest first.

decisions.description:
Decisions are the decisions whose depends names the uri, the latest version
of each.

evaluations.description:
Evaluations are the evaluations whose depends names it, the latest filing
of each Evaluation Run.

newest.description: Newest is the hash of its newest version. Empty when none is filed.

uri.description: URI is the evidence asked about.

data.description: Data are the evaluations, newest first.

Data are the versions, newest first. Content is left out; read one by id
for it.

id.description: ID is the experiment stable id whose retained versions are listed.

project.description: Project is the project scope the returned versions belong to.

versions.description:
Versions are every retained version of the experiment ordered ascending by seq,
proving whether a planning/running pre-registration preceded its complete result.

data.description: Data are the canonical experiment versions.

total.description: Total is len(data) — the rows in this answer, not the store's history.

updated.description: Updated is the number of records the grant applied to. Zero is a 404, never a silent no-op.

data.description: Data are the pre-registered hypotheses, newest sequence number first.

attempts_ingested.description: AttemptsIngested is how many attempt versions this call appended.

attempts_retained.description: AttemptsRetained is the full versioned attempt history the store now holds.

canonical_attempts.description: CanonicalAttempts is the deduped attempt count the store now holds.

canonical_experiments.description: CanonicalExperiments is the deduped experiment count the store now holds.

experiments_ingested.description: ExperimentsIngested is how many experiment versions this call appended.

experiments_retained.description: ExperimentsRetained is the full versioned experiment history the store now holds.

project.description: Project is the project the batch was filed under — the SERVER's value, never the body's.

rolled_up.description: RolledUp is false when the OLAP roll-up was skipped; the SQLite write still stands.

papers.description:
Papers are the writings to record. Each needs an id. At most 20000 in
one call.

data.description: Data are the canonical papers, ordered by project then id.
Data are the org's projects with canonical + retained counts.

evidence_refs.description: EvidenceRefs lists the holdout Evidence or Run digests establishing fitness.

evolution_fitness.description: EvolutionFitness is the optional Level 2 meta-evolutionary fitness vector.

id.description: ID is the target candidate's sha256:... candidate_id from the URL path.

product_fitness.description: ProductFitness is the verified Level 1 fitness vector measured by the qualifier.

promote.description:
Promote transitions the candidate directly to promoted when true; otherwise
status becomes qualified.

rollback_target.description:
RollbackTarget names the pinned parent candidate_id or baseline artifact
digest to roll back to if post-promotion monitoring regresses; defaults to parent_ids[0].

signature.description: Signature is the qualifier's optional cryptographic signature over candidate_id.

canonical.description:
Canonical is how many distinct records of this kind the store now holds
— the deduped view, retractions withdrawn.

project.description:
Project is the project the batch was filed under — the SERVER's value,
never the body's.

recorded.description:
Recorded is how many NEW versions this call appended. Zero on a
byte-identical re-send, which is what makes a backfill replayable.

data.description: Data are the canonical RegressionRecords, newest sequence number first.

confidence_hi.description: ConfidenceHi is the optional upper confidence bound of the replication run.

confidence_lo.description: ConfidenceLo is the optional lower confidence bound of the replication run.

id.description: ID is the target claim's sha256:... claim_id from the URL path.

run_id.description: RunID is the completed independent clean-room Run reproducing the claim.

tolerance.description:
Tolerance is the maximum absolute difference permitted when neither run
carries confidence intervals; defaults to 0.05 (5% relative or absolute).

value.description:
Value is the optional replication measurement when the run's measures array
omits the named metric.

evidence_ref.description:
EvidenceRef is the content-addressed Evidence or artifact digest proving the
refutation or post-deployment regression.

id.description: ID is the target claim or candidate sha256:... identifier from the URL path.

run_id.description: RunID is the optional completed Run ID demonstrating the refutation.

summary.description: Summary explains concisely why the prior claim or candidate is retracted.

runs.description:
Runs are the executions to record. Each needs an id and a benchmark. A
system is not required: a tree that does not name what was under test
cannot be made to, and demanding the field is how one gets invented. At
most 20000 in one call.

completion.description:
Completion counts the matched runs, across every page, by completion.
Read it before reading any aggregate over Data: a set whose Unknown or
Partial is a large share of Total is a set whose average is over runs
that may not have finished.

data.description:
Data are the canonical runs, each with its derived completion, ordered
by project then id: one page of them.

gaps.description:
Gaps is one field per entry that some matched run leaves unstated, with
how many leave it unstated, worst first. It is the record's account of
its own incompleteness, and it is answered on every listing rather than
discovered by reading the rows: a field nobody records is a comparison
nobody can make.

next.description:
Next continues the listing: pass it back as `cursor`. Absent on the last
page.

total.description: Total is how many runs the query matched, across every page.

completion.description: Completion counts the matched runs, across every page, by completion.

data.description:
Data are the canonical runs, ordered by project then id, each as the
summary view serves it: one page of them.

next.description:
Next continues the listing: pass it back as `cursor`. Absent on the last
page.

total.description: Total is how many runs the query matched, across every page.

data.description: Data are the canonical studies, ordered by project then id.

studies.description:
Studies are the inquiries to record. Each needs an id. At most 20000 in
one call.

commit.description:
Commit is the project commit they were read at: lowercase hex, no prefix.
Required.

elements.description:
Elements are SysML v2 API JSON elements: each has `@id` and `@type`, and a
relationship has `source`/`target` or `relatedElement`, arrays of
{"@id"}. At most 20000, counting with the elements every link a Satisfy,
Verify, Derive, Refine or Dependency relationship names: each of its
sources to each of its targets.

project.description:
Project is the SysML project the elements belong to, without `@` or `#`,
which delimit an element's uri. Required.

balances.description: Balances lists per-principal domain XP totals sorted by total_xp descending.

non_transferable.description:
NonTransferable is always true: Hanzo XP is soulbound reputation, never a
transferable token or currency (HIP-1402 §1).

projections.description: Projections lists every deterministic XPProjection event folded into Balances.

rule_version.description: RuleVersion is the semantic version of the deterministic projection rules ("1.0.0").

bearer.description: The caller's credential, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. It is either an access token minted by Hanzo IAM or an API key (pk-/sk-). X-Authorization, and HTTP Basic carrying the token as the password, are accepted spellings of the same header for clients that cannot set Authorization; a browser presents the session cookie instead. Every operation requires it unless it says `security: []`.
